subject: BAR
title: City of Marlow Heights: Governmental Fund Statements and Fund Balance Classification
scenario:
The City of Marlow Heights has a fiscal year that ends on June 30. You are assisting the City's finance department in preparing the governmental fund financial statements for the fiscal year ended June 30, Year 2 (Year 2). The financial statements will be issued on September 15, Year 2.

The City reports three governmental funds: the General Fund, the Street Maintenance Fund (a special revenue fund), and the Cemetery Perpetual Care Fund (a permanent fund). The City also operates a water utility reported as an enterprise fund.

Balance sheet data for the funds at June 30, Year 2, appear in **Exhibit 1**. Excerpts from City Council actions, agreements, and management designations appear in **Exhibit 2**. General Fund activity for Year 2 appears in **Exhibit 3**. All transactions in Exhibit 3 have been reflected in the balances in Exhibit 1. Unless a task states otherwise, answer in whole dollars.

exhibits.title: Exhibit 2: Council Actions, Agreements, and Designations
exhibits.content:
**1. Street Maintenance Fund (special revenue fund).** City Ordinance 88 levies a $25 local vehicle registration fee and requires that the fee revenue be used only for street maintenance. Under state law, residents may compel the City to use the fee revenue for that purpose. At June 30, Year 2, the fund's resources other than its road salt inventory consist of $162,000 derived from registration fees and $55,000 derived from transfers from the General Fund. On May 14, Year 2, the City Council adopted a resolution committing $30,000 of the transfer-derived resources to a bridge inspection program. No other action has been taken regarding the transfer-derived resources; public works staff expect to spend them on street maintenance.

**2. Cemetery Perpetual Care Fund (permanent fund).** Under the terms of a bequest, the $400,000 principal must be maintained in perpetuity, and investment earnings may be spent only for maintenance of the municipal cemetery. During Year 2, $28,000 of earnings was transferred to the General Fund, which performs the cemetery maintenance.

**3. State body-camera grant.** In March, Year 2, the State paid the City $100,000 under a grant agreement that requires the money to be spent on police body cameras. The grant has no eligibility requirements other than this purpose restriction. By June 30, Year 2, $30,000 had been spent. Purchase orders for body cameras outstanding at June 30, Year 2, total $18,000.

**4. Loan to Marlow Housing Partnership.** The General Fund loaned $90,000 to a local nonprofit housing organization. The loan is due in full in Year 7. Repayments will be available to the General Fund for general operations.

**5. City Council resolutions affecting the General Fund.** The City Charter designates the City Council as the City's highest level of decision-making authority. Commitments are established by Council resolution and can be modified or rescinded only by Council resolution.

| Date adopted | Resolution |
| --- | --- |
| June 12, Year 2 | Commits $250,000 to replacement of the emergency dispatch system |
| June 25, Year 2 | Commits the portion of Year 2 sales tax collections in excess of the budgeted amount to storm-drain rehabilitation. On August 10, Year 2, the Finance Department determined the amount to be $45,000. |
| July 21, Year 2 | Commits $60,000 to park lighting improvements |

**6. Year 3 budget.** On June 20, Year 2, the City Council adopted the Year 3 General Fund budget, with estimated revenues of $8,210,000 and appropriations of $8,330,000. The budget appropriates $120,000 of existing General Fund fund balance to eliminate the projected deficit.

**7. Delegated authority.** A City ordinance authorizes the Finance Director to assign fund balance to specific purposes. On June 28, Year 2, the Finance Director assigned $35,000 of General Fund fund balance to a Year 3 upgrade of the financial reporting software.

**8. General Fund encumbrances outstanding at June 30, Year 2.** Public works equipment, $28,000 (not subject to any restriction or commitment); police body cameras, $18,000 (see item 3).

exhibits.title: Exhibit 3: General Fund Activity for Year 2
exhibits.content:
**Revenues recognized (modified accrual basis)**

| Source | Amount |
| --- | --- |
| Property taxes | $5,200,000 |
| Sales taxes | 1,480,000 |
| Intergovernmental (includes the $100,000 State body-camera grant) | 820,000 |
| Licenses, fines, and charges for services | 450,000 |

**Current expenditures** (exclude the capital outlay and debt service transactions described below)

| Function | Amount |
| --- | --- |
| General government | $1,406,750 |
| Public safety | 3,960,000 |
| Public works | 1,540,000 |
| Culture and recreation | 650,000 |

**Other transactions**

a. **Series A general obligation serial bonds.** The bonds bear interest at 5%, payable January 1 and July 1. Principal of $150,000 matures each July 1. Outstanding principal at June 30, Year 1, was $1,200,000. The City made every payment on its due date. The City does not use a debt service fund; general obligation debt is serviced directly from the General Fund, and no resources have been set aside in advance for the July 1, Year 2, payment.

b. **New bond issue.** On February 1, Year 2, the City issued $500,000 of 10-year, 4% general obligation bonds at 102. Interest is payable February 1 and August 1, beginning August 1, Year 2. In February, Year 2, the City used the proceeds to purchase land for a future park at a cost of $510,000. The City does not use a capital projects fund for single-asset acquisitions.

c. **Equipment lease.** On June 1, Year 2, the City entered into a 5-year lease of street-sweeping equipment. Five annual payments of $34,000 are due beginning June 1, Year 3. At the 5% discount rate, the present value of the lease payments at commencement is $147,202. The lease does not transfer ownership, and no payment was made during Year 2.

d. **Sale of surplus vehicles.** The City sold surplus police vehicles for $45,000 cash. The government-wide records show an original cost of $160,000 and accumulated depreciation of $130,000.

e. **Transfer in** of $28,000 from the Cemetery Perpetual Care Fund (see Exhibit 2, item 2).

f. **Transfer out** of $80,000 to the Street Maintenance Fund.

g. **Tax anticipation notes.** On April 1, Year 2, the City issued $300,000 of 4% tax anticipation notes due September 30, Year 2, with interest payable at maturity. The $3,000 of interest accrued at June 30, Year 2, is included in general government expenditures above.

h. **General Fund fund balance at July 1, Year 1:** $1,420,000.

tasks.title: Other Financing Sources — General Fund
tasks.instruction: Using Exhibit 3, calculate the total other financing sources that the City should report in the General Fund column of the statement of revenues, expenditures, and changes in fund balances for Year 2. Enter the amount in whole dollars (in whole dollars, no commas).
tasks.explanation:
Other financing sources in a governmental fund include the face amount of long-term debt issued, any issuance premium, the amount recognized for a lease at commencement, proceeds from sales of capital assets, and transfers in.

- Face amount of general obligation bonds: $500,000
- Bond premium ($500,000 × 102% − $500,000): $10,000
- Lease at commencement (present value of lease payments): $147,202
- Proceeds from sale of surplus vehicles: $45,000
- Transfer in from the Cemetery Perpetual Care Fund: $28,000

Total other financing sources = $730,202.

The $300,000 of tax anticipation notes is a short-term fund liability (reported on the General Fund balance sheet), not an other financing source. The $80,000 transfer out is an other financing use. The vehicles' original cost and accumulated depreciation affect only the government-wide statements; the fund reports the cash proceeds.
tasks.explanationJa:
**考え方**: 政府ファンド（修正発生主義）では、長期の資金調達は負債ではなく「その他の財源（Other financing sources）」として変動計算書に計上する。

| 項目 | 金額 | 扱い |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GO債の額面 | $500,000 | 含める |
| 発行プレミアム（$500,000 × 102% − $500,000） | $10,000 | 含める（償却しない） |
| リース開始時の計上額（リース料の現在価値） | $147,202 | 含める |
| 余剰車両の売却代金 | $45,000 | 含める（ファンドは受取額を計上。原価・減価償却累計額は政府全体の財務諸表だけで使う） |
| 永久基金からの振替入 | $28,000 | 含める |
| TAN（税収見合いの短期借入）$300,000 | — | 含めない（一般基金の貸借対照表の流動負債） |
| 道路維持基金への振替出 $80,000 | — | 含めない（その他の使途 = Other financing uses） |

**合計**: $500,000 + $10,000 + $147,202 + $45,000 + $28,000 = **$730,202**

ポイント: TANは翌期中に税収で返済する短期借入なので、ファンドの負債として計上し、財源にはしない。

tasks.title: Debt Service Expenditures on General Obligation Bonds
tasks.instruction: Using Exhibit 3, calculate the total debt service expenditures (principal and interest) on general obligation bonds that the City should report in the General Fund for Year 2. Enter the amount in whole dollars (in whole dollars, no commas).
tasks.explanation:
Under the modified accrual basis, principal and interest on general long-term debt are recognized as expenditures when due (the matured amount), not as interest accrues. Because the City does not use a debt service fund and has not set aside resources in advance, the optional early recognition of the July 1, Year 2, installment is not available.

Series A bonds:
- July 1, Year 1: principal $150,000 + interest ($1,200,000 × 5% × 6/12) $30,000
- January 1, Year 2: interest ($1,050,000 × 5% × 6/12) $26,250

Total = $150,000 + $30,000 + $26,250 = $206,250.

Not recognized in Year 2: the July 1, Year 2, installment (principal $150,000 and interest $26,250) and interest on the new 4% bonds for February 1 through June 30, Year 2 (first payment due August 1, Year 2). Interest on the tax anticipation notes is a fund liability and is already included in current expenditures, not in debt service on general obligation bonds.
tasks.explanationJa:
**考え方**: 修正発生主義では、一般長期債務の元利は**支払期日が到来した時点**で支出（Expenditures—debt service）を認識する。期間の経過で利息を未払計上しない。

**ステップ1: 当期（Year 1年7/1〜Year 2年6/30）に支払期日が来る支払いを拾う**

| 支払期日 | 元本 | 利息 | 計算 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Year 1年7/1 | $150,000 | $30,000 | $1,200,000 × 5% × 6/12 |
| Year 2年1/1 | — | $26,250 | ($1,200,000 − $150,000) × 5% × 6/12 |

**ステップ2: 合計** $150,000 + $30,000 + $26,250 = **$206,250**

**当期の支出にしないもの**
- Year 2年7/1 の元本 $150,000・利息 $26,250（期日は翌期。債務返済基金へ事前に財源を移していないので、前倒し計上の例外も使えない）
- 新規4%債の 2/1〜6/30 の経過利息（初回利払いは Year 2年8/1）
- TANの未払利息 $3,000（短期のファンド負債。一般行政費に含まれており、GO債の元利ではない）

tasks.title: Total Expenditures — General Fund
tasks.instruction: Using Exhibit 3, calculate the total expenditures (current, capital outlay, and debt service) that the City should report in the General Fund for Year 2. Enter the amount in whole dollars (in whole dollars, no commas).
tasks.explanation:
Current expenditures: $1,406,750 + $3,960,000 + $1,540,000 + $650,000 = $7,556,750.

Capital outlay: land purchased with bond proceeds $510,000 + leased equipment recognized at commencement $147,202 = $657,202. At lease commencement, a governmental fund reports a capital outlay expenditure and an other financing source for the same amount, even though no cash is paid.

Debt service on general obligation bonds (Work Tab 2): $206,250.

Total expenditures = $7,556,750 + $657,202 + $206,250 = $8,420,202.

Reconciliation to the balance sheet: revenues $7,950,000 − expenditures $8,420,202 + other financing sources $730,202 − other financing uses $80,000 = net change of $180,000. Beginning fund balance $1,420,000 + $180,000 = $1,600,000, which equals General Fund assets $2,318,000 − liabilities $583,000 − deferred inflows $135,000.
tasks.explanationJa:
**ステップ1: 経常的支出（current）**
$1,406,750 + $3,960,000 + $1,540,000 + $650,000 = $7,556,750

**ステップ2: 資本的支出（capital outlay）**
- 起債収入で購入した土地: $510,000（ファンドでは資産計上せず支出にする）
- リース開始時の計上額: $147,202（現金支払いがなくても、開始時に「支出（capital outlay）」と「その他の財源」を同額で両建てする）
- 合計 $657,202

**ステップ3: 債務返済（debt service）** — Work Tab 2 の $206,250

**合計**: $7,556,750 + $657,202 + $206,250 = **$8,420,202**

**貸借対照表との突き合わせ（検算）**

| 項目 | 金額 |
| --- | --- |
| 歳入 | $7,950,000 |
| 歳出 | ($8,420,202) |
| その他の財源 | $730,202 |
| その他の使途（振替出） | ($80,000) |
| ファンド残高の増減 | $180,000 |
| 期首ファンド残高 | $1,420,000 |
| 期末ファンド残高 | $1,600,000 |

Exhibit 1 の資産 $2,318,000 − 負債 $583,000 − 繰延流入 $135,000 = $1,600,000 と一致する。

tasks.title: Fund Balance Classification by Fund
tasks.instruction: Using Exhibits 1 and 2, complete the fund balance section of the governmental funds balance sheet at June 30, Year 2. For each fund, enter the amount of each fund balance classification and the total fund balance in whole dollars, with no commas. Enter 0 for any classification that has no amount. If a classification is a deficit, enter it as a negative number.
tasks.explanation:
Total fund balance for each fund equals assets minus liabilities minus deferred inflows of resources: General Fund $2,318,000 − $583,000 − $135,000 = $1,600,000; Street Maintenance Fund $268,000 − $33,000 = $235,000; Cemetery Perpetual Care Fund $445,000.

General Fund:
- Nonspendable: inventories $64,000 + prepaid insurance $22,000 + long-term loan receivable $90,000 = $176,000. The loan is nonspendable because repayments are not restricted, committed, or assigned.
- Restricted: unspent State grant $100,000 − $30,000 = $70,000 (constraint imposed by the grantor). The $18,000 body-camera encumbrance is included in this amount, not added to assigned.
- Committed: dispatch system $250,000 + storm-drain rehabilitation $45,000 = $295,000. A commitment must be made by the highest decision-making authority by year-end; the amount may be determined after year-end. The July 21, Year 2, resolution was adopted after year-end and is not a commitment at June 30, Year 2.
- Assigned: appropriation of existing fund balance in the adopted Year 3 budget $120,000 + Finance Director's assignment under delegated authority $35,000 + unconstrained public works encumbrance $28,000 = $183,000.
- Unassigned: $1,600,000 − $176,000 − $70,000 − $295,000 − $183,000 = $876,000.

Street Maintenance Fund:
- Nonspendable: road salt inventory $18,000.
- Restricted: registration-fee resources $162,000. Enabling legislation that is legally enforceable creates a restriction.
- Committed: bridge inspection resolution $30,000.
- Assigned: remaining transfer-derived resources $55,000 − $30,000 = $25,000. In a governmental fund other than the General Fund, the remaining positive amount that is not restricted or committed is assigned.
- Unassigned: $0. Only the General Fund reports positive unassigned fund balance; other governmental funds report unassigned fund balance only as a deficit.

Cemetery Perpetual Care Fund:
- Nonspendable: principal required to be maintained intact $400,000.
- Restricted: earnings restricted by the bequest to cemetery maintenance $445,000 − $400,000 = $45,000.
tasks.explanationJa:
**ステップ1: 各ファンドのファンド残高総額（資産 − 負債 − 繰延流入）**
- 一般基金: $2,318,000 − $583,000 − $135,000 = $1,600,000（未収固定資産税の繰延流入はファンド残高ではない）
- 道路維持基金: $268,000 − $33,000 = $235,000
- 墓地永代管理基金: $445,000

**ステップ2: 一般基金の区分**

| 区分 | 内訳 | 金額 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Nonspendable | 棚卸資産 $64,000 + 前払保険料 $22,000 + 長期貸付金 $90,000 | $176,000 |
| Restricted | 州補助金の未使用分 $100,000 − $30,000（補助金提供者による外部制約） | $70,000 |
| Committed | 通信指令システム $250,000 + 雨水管改修 $45,000 | $295,000 |
| Assigned | Year 3 予算での既存残高の充当 $120,000 + 財務部長の指定 $35,000 + 発注残（公共事業設備）$28,000 | $183,000 |
| Unassigned | 残余 $1,600,000 − 上記合計 | $876,000 |

- 長期貸付金は返済金の使途に制約がないので nonspendable（restricted ではない）。
- ボディカメラの発注残 $18,000 は restricted $70,000 の内数。assigned に二重計上しない。
- 雨水管改修は期末前（6/25）に議会が決議しているので committed。金額が期末後に確定しても構わない。
- 公園照明（7/21 決議）は期末後の決議なので、期末時点では committed にならず unassigned に残る。
- 翌期予算の赤字補填のための既存残高の充当は、議会の行為でも **assigned**（committed ではない）。
- 財務部長は条例で権限を委任されているので、その指定は assigned。

**ステップ3: 道路維持基金（特別収入基金）の区分**

| 区分 | 内訳 | 金額 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Nonspendable | 融雪用塩の在庫 | $18,000 |
| Restricted | 登録料由来の資源（授権条例 = enabling legislation による法的強制力のある制約） | $162,000 |
| Committed | 橋梁点検の議会決議 | $30,000 |
| Assigned | 振替由来 $55,000 − $30,000 | $25,000 |
| Unassigned | — | $0 |

- 自らの条例でも、法的に強制できる授権法による制約は **restricted**。
- 一般基金以外の政府ファンドでは、restricted・committed に当たらない**プラスの残余は assigned**。unassigned はマイナス（赤字）のときだけ使う。

**ステップ4: 墓地永代管理基金（永久基金）の区分**
- Nonspendable: 永久に維持すべき元本 $400,000
- Restricted: 運用益 $445,000 − $400,000 = $45,000（遺贈条件で墓地管理に限定）

tasks.title: Committed Fund Balance — General Fund
tasks.instruction: Using Exhibit 2, select all items that the City should report as committed fund balance in the General Fund at June 30, Year 2.
options: Dispatch system replacement resolution adopted June 12, Year 2
Storm-drain rehabilitation resolution adopted June 25, Year 2
Park lighting resolution adopted July 21, Year 2
Appropriation of existing fund balance in the adopted Year 3 budget
Finance Director's assignment for the software upgrade
correctAnswer: Dispatch system replacement resolution adopted June 12, Year 2
Storm-drain rehabilitation resolution adopted June 25, Year 2
tasks.explanation:
Committed fund balance results from formal action of the government's highest level of decision-making authority, taken before the end of the reporting period, that can be changed only by the same type of action.

- Dispatch system resolution (June 12, Year 2): committed.
- Storm-drain resolution (June 25, Year 2): committed. The formal action occurred before year-end; the amount may be determined after year-end.
- Park lighting resolution (July 21, Year 2): not committed at June 30, Year 2, because the action was taken after year-end.
- Appropriation of existing fund balance to eliminate a projected deficit in the subsequent year's budget: assigned, not committed.
- Finance Director's assignment: assigned, because it expresses the intent of an official with delegated authority.
- Unspent State grant: restricted, because the constraint is imposed by an external party.
tasks.explanationJa:
**Committed の要件**: 最高意思決定機関（本問では市議会）が、**期末日までに**正式な行為（決議）で使途を拘束し、変更・撤回にも同じ種類の行為が必要なもの。

| 項目 | 区分 | 理由 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 通信指令システム（6/12 決議） | **Committed** | 期末前の議会決議 |
| 雨水管改修（6/25 決議） | **Committed** | 決議は期末前。金額が期末後（8/10）に確定しても committed になる |
| 公園照明（7/21 決議） | Unassigned | 決議が期末後なので期末時点では拘束されていない |
| Year 3 予算での既存残高の充当 | Assigned | 翌期予算の赤字補填のための充当は GASB 54 で assigned と定められている |
| 財務部長の指定 | Assigned | 委任を受けた職員の意図の表明 |
| 州補助金の未使用分 | Restricted | 外部（補助金提供者）が課した制約 |

よく出る誤り: 「議会が関わっている = committed」と覚えると、予算での充当を committed にしてしまう。また、決議日が期末の前か後かを必ず確認すること。

tasks.title: Modifying a Commitment
tasks.instruction: In November, Year 2, the City Council wants to redirect $100,000 of the amount committed to the emergency dispatch system to park lighting improvements. Based on Exhibit 2, select the action required for the $100,000 to be removed from the dispatch system commitment.
options: Adoption of a new City Council resolution, the same type of formal action used to establish the commitment
A written reassignment by the Finance Director under the delegated-authority ordinance
Approval by the State, because committed amounts are constraints imposed by an external party
No formal action; management may reclassify committed amounts at year-end based on its current intentions
tasks.correctAnswer: Adoption of a new City Council resolution, the same type of formal action used to establish the commitment
tasks.explanation:
Amounts in committed fund balance cannot be used for any other purpose unless the government removes or changes the constraint by taking the same type of action it used to commit the amounts. The City Charter provides that commitments are established by Council resolution and can be modified or rescinded only by Council resolution, so a new Council resolution is required.

The Finance Director's delegated authority extends only to assigning fund balance; an official cannot remove a commitment. Committed amounts are self-imposed by the government's highest decision-making authority, not imposed by the State (externally imposed constraints produce restricted fund balance). Management's changing intentions affect assigned amounts, not committed amounts.
tasks.explanationJa:
**結論**: 議会の**新たな決議**（拘束を設けたときと同じ種類の正式な行為）が必要。

- Committed は、設定したときと同じ種類の行為でなければ変更・撤回できない。本問では市憲章が「決議で設定し、決議でのみ変更・撤回できる」と定めている。
- 財務部長が委任されているのは **assign** の権限だけ。職員が議会の拘束を外すことはできない。
- 州の承認が必要なのは外部から課された制約（restricted）の場合。committed は政府自身が課した制約。
- 経営者の意図の変化で動かせるのは assigned であり、committed ではない。

対比して覚える: restricted = 外部または法的強制力のある授権法 / committed = 議会の正式決議（撤回も同じ手続き）/ assigned = 権限を持つ機関・職員の意図。
